hypotheses.justification: The conclusion only concerns g acting on V, and X appears elsewhere in the statement only through e : elementaryGroup Q →* X. Since F is finite and V is finite-dimensional, V is finite, so V ≃ₗ[F] V and hence elementaryGroup Q are finite. So e.range is finite, whatever X is. `Finite X` is used in the proof only through commutator_img_eq_bot and then Orth15Alpha.commutator_eq_bot_of_layers [Finite G]. In that lemma, `Finite G` is used for exactly one thing: giving `Finite ↥H` to le_center_of_odd_normal (it is also an instance argument elsewhere, but not used in the argument). Here every layer H satisfies H ≤ P = img e (elemOn Q S ⊔ elemOn Q T) ≤ e.range, so each H is finite anyway. So the hypothesis can be weakened in the lemma to 'each H ∈ 𝓗 is finite', or equivalently 'P is finite', and the finiteness of H supplied from the finiteness of e.range. The rest of the lemma (commutator manipulations, Odd (Nat.card O) divisibility) does not use finiteness of G. The statement remains true for infinite X: odd Nat.card N forces N finite, and all the data live in the finite subgroup e.range. The remaining steps (preserves_of_odd, commute_join_of_odd's key argument, exists_smul_of_commute_elemOn) never use Finite X. The other hypotheses are used.
